merge_guidance.reason: The matrix now covers 70 applied packets from note 849 through note 981; the latest packet is 981 (NYC MyCity local digital administrative service-home stress test). The dominant form families are: thick functional authority (1); thin connector / shared-service backbone (1); middle regional risk platform (1); asset-heavy regional utility authority (1); contract-heavy public delivery authority / P3 crossing authority (1); regulatory/enforcement coordination waist (1); treaty/global narrow-waist institution (1); procedural digital / interoperability assessment waist (1); 62 other families. The chain is manual-ready but not deletion-ready because apparent overlap often hides different affected-party tails, repair surfaces, source postures, or anti-theater tests. Keep the case packets until a merge review proves that no live dispatch, source-currentness, appeal, compensation, degraded-mode, or tail-risk function would be lost.

consolidation_map.instruction: use the dispatcher, manual, and defeat tests as the first-entry route before any chain note is cited
keep as the form-choice ladder inside the manual; do not bury the minimum-sufficient-form question
draft as the manual core only while preserving fiscal, oversight, participation, and redress tests
merge with strong examples because public record and membership surfaces are common but not equally heavy in thin cases
keep visibly separate; each protects a distinct heavy-power path that can be hidden by generic connector language
add explicit soft-law-hardening and database-alert tests to prevent recommendations, ratings, alerts, and data systems from becoming hidden authority
add authority-lane, consent / co-decision, legal-person, retained-state-duty, public-rights, and remedy tests when Indigenous authority, legal personality, or relational territory is live

add public-owner, processor, admin-access, product-purpose, benefit-proof, opposition, fallback, and exit-rehearsal tests when cloud, SaaS, AI, identity, analytics, or platform suppliers become public-service infrastructure

add legal-trigger, active-power, waiver, reactivation, local-capacity, service-continuity, record-publication, democratic-damage, and final-release tests when fiscal distress, receivership, state oversight, devolution, or handback is live

add mandate-owner, resource-control, data-reality, contract-traceability, provider-dependence, principal-accountability, attribution-boundary, transition-receipt, and recharter-choice tests when a visible body is credited, blamed, abolished, absorbed, or expanded for a public outcome whose operative levers sit elsewhere

add mandate-capacity, host-owner, pledge-to-deployment, access-class, civilian-harm, humanitarian-boundary, justice-chain, private-force, emergency-record, and handback-ladder tests when fragile-jurisdiction or donor-dependent support arrangements are treated as operative authority

add legal-authority, evidentiary-proxy, burden, data-lineage, human-determination, notice / explanation, review / stay, vulnerability, business-rule scrutiny, and remediation-loop tests when data matches, models, rule engines, scores, calculators, workflows, or AI systems may create legal or similarly significant public effects

add public-owner, canonical-corpus, source-trace, reliance-warning, answer-consistency, accessibility, correction-clock, incident-disclosure, supplier / model-change, human-handoff, and withdrawal / transition-receipt tests when public chatbots, RAG assistants, service bots, or generated guidance shape conduct or service access without a formal decision
